papers.title: Balancing adversariality and naturalness in autonomous vehicle testing scenario generation via multi-objective reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL)-based adversarial scenario generation through dynamic agent-environment interactions has emerged as a promising approach for accelerating autonomous vehicle (AV) testing. However, existing RL approaches struggle to balance adversariality and naturalness because naturalistic driving behaviors avoid risk whereas adversarial behaviors intentionally induce it. The reward-driven nature of RL can further lead to objective polarization under linearly weighted rewards, resulting in scenarios biased toward a limited range of adversariality-naturalness trade-offs. papers.title: DA-RL: decoupled attention-enhanced visual feature reinforcement learning for optimised decision-making in cyber-physical systems
papers.summary: In dynamic and complex environments, visual reinforcement learning (Visual RL) agents struggle to extract task-relevant information, achieve stable policy optimisation, and generalise across changing conditions. This paper proposes DA-RL, an attention-enhanced and decoupled reinforcement learning framework for cyber-physical decision-making. An attention-based encoder highlights critical environmental cues, while decoupled feature and policy optimisation improves training stability and convergence efficiency. papers.title: Digital and Intelligent Technologies for Construction and Demolition Waste Sorting: A Systematic Mapping Review of Research Maturity, Circularity Outcomes, and Industry Gaps
papers.summary: Construction and demolition waste (CDW) sorting is increasingly supported by digital and intelligent technologies, yet their functional coverage, maturity, circular economy (CE) contribution and alignment with industrial practice remain fragmented. This review systematically mapped the field using a PRISMA-based search, with 396 publications forming the broader bibliometric corpus. Within this corpus, 204 publications were retained for the scoped review, comprising 185 primary technical studies and 19 review articles. papers.title: Bio-inspired flexible pressure sensors: morphology-guided structure–function relationships, reliability, and future perspectives
papers.summary: Bio-inspired flexible pressure sensors have emerged as a major class of soft sensing systems for wearable electronics, electronic skin, human–machine interfaces, and soft robotics because biological structures provide effective design principles for regulating deformation, contact evolution, and interfacial adaptation. papers.title: Cross-robot open-set fault detection via normal-only adaptation and residual latent-space alignment
papers.summary: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a cross-robot framework for open-set fault detection using only normal data from the target robot. papers.title: RSAC: Robotic Surgery Adaptive Curricula
papers.summary: Robotic Surgery Adaptive Curricula (RSAC) is software for generating individualised, adaptive training pathways in robotic surgery simulation. After each recorded attempt, it evaluates data sufficiency and performance trajectories relative to predefined proficiency thresholds, then recommends whether the trainee should repeat the current exercise, advance through standard or accelerated progression, move to an exercise of comparable difficulty, or return to a simpler exercise for remediation. papers.title: A Gateway-Based Approach for Integrating Digital Compass Data into Controller Area Network (CAN) in Precision Farming Systems
papers.summary: The integration of high precision orientation sensors into resilient communication infrastructures is a key requirement for next-generation autonomous systems. Digital compass sensors typically generate data in the NMEA format, whereas distributed control architectures in mobile robotics predominantly utilize the CAN 2.0B protocol. This study presents the design and implementation of a microcontroller-based hardware-software gateway that enables seamless interoperability between these heterogeneous communication standards within autonomous agricultural platforms. papers.title: Coaxially 3D‐Printed Dual‐Mode Magnetoelectric Fiber Sensors for Robotic Manipulator Proprioception
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Flexible sensors for robotic proprioception are often limited by single transduction pathways and multistep fabrication/assembly strategies, making it difficult to simultaneously achieve integrated static–dynamic motion sensing and structurally continuous deformable devices. Here, we report a coaxially 3D‐printed dual‐mode magnetoelectric fiber sensor (DMEFS) with a helical liquid‐metal core/magnetic‐elastomer sheath architecture. The customized coaxial printing and winding strategy enables direct integration of conductive and magnetic functionalities within one fiber‐like structure.

papers.title: Rules or Character? Scaling Laws for AI Safety Design (Extended Abstract)
papers.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) safety systems combine character shaping (e.g., Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback [RLHF], Constitutional AI), which modifies behavioral distributions at training time, with rule enforcement (e.g., output filters, safety classifiers), which blocks harmful outputs at inference time, yet little formal analysis exists on how their optimal balance should change as deployment scales increase. papers.title: Survival-aware self-play reinforcement learning for partially observable beyond visual range air combat
papers.summary: We present a recurrent self-play reinforcement learning framework for autonomous beyond-visual-range (BVR) air combat under partial observability. The environment is formulated as a decision-level BVR missile-duel simulator that combines 3-DoF aircraft kinematics, field-of-view radar observation, track-quality decay, flight-envelope action masking, and an energy-aware missile model with boost, coast, drag, and proportional-navigation guidance. papers.title: Virtue by Observation: Social Reinforcement Learning for Intrinsically Ethical Agents
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning is increasingly deployed in settings with ethical stakes, yet rule-based and scalar-reward alignment approaches remain brittle and prone to proxy gaming. I argue that two of their most persistent failures, hallucination and moral drift, share a single structural cause, which I term \textit{feedback collapse}: the compression of plural human values into a static scalar reward by a fixed evaluation model. My research develops a virtue-centric alternative, Social Reinforcement Learning, in which evaluative authority is distributed across a dynamic population of peer agents.

papers.title: AI Alignment Without Representation: From Scalar Rewards to Social Deliberation
papers.summary: Despite the widespread adoption of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, state-of-the-art AI systems remain prone to two persistent failures. The first is hallucination, or the production of fluent but false content. The second is moral drift, or the convergence toward exploitative or harmful equilibria under sustained deployment. We argue that these are not distinct pathologies but may arise from a single structural cause that we term feedback collapse. papers.title: A representation of the visual environment in the human basolateral amygdala supports learning and choice
papers.summary: Animals continuously transform sensory inputs into representations that guide behavior. Although the amygdala is a brain structure critical for learning and choice, how natural sensory experience is represented within this circuit remains unknown. Here, we identify a representation of the visual environment in the human basolateral amygdala (BLA) that contains information relevant for learning and choice. papers.title: Superquadric primitive decomposition of 3D point clouds via geometric-aware inlier refinement
papers.summary: The decomposition of 3D point clouds into interpretable geometric primitives remains a longstanding challenge in Computer Vision and Computer Graphics. Among the available representations, superquadrics offer a compact and expressive model capable of capturing a wide range of shapes. However, their estimation is inherently challenging, as it requires solving a non-linear optimization problem and is particularly sensitive to noise, outliers, and overlapping structures. papers.title: A Computer Vision-Based Driver Drowsiness Detection System Using Facial Landmarks and Temporal Eye Analysis
papers.summary: Driver drowsiness is an important traffic safety problem, as reduced alertness is known to affect visual attention, decision making and reaction time thereby increasing the risk of unsafe driving. Continuous monitoring of driver behavior can help identify visual signals that are associated with drowsiness and provide feedback to the driver in a timely manner. In this paper, we present a web CV driver monitoring system that focuses on drowsiness detection based on facial landmarks and temporal eye behavior. papers.title: Main Dataset(Gazebo-Based Aerial Target Detection Dataset for UAV Research)
papers.summary: Gazebo-Based Aerial Target Detection Dataset This dataset contains 1,344 simulated aerial target images generated by the authors in the Gazebo simulation environment for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) object detection research. It includes three aerial vehicle classes: x4_uav, x3_uav, and fixed_wing. The images were collected from different camera perspectives, including side and top views, under varying flight scenarios, target positions, distances, and motion conditions. papers.title: Manipulation-Proof Oblivious Audits Against Deceptive Model Providers
papers.summary: Audits have emerged as a critical instrument for algorithmic governance, providing a mechanism for external scrutiny and governance of machine learning models. However, ensuring the integrity of such assessments remains a challenging issue. For instance in regulatory contexts, audits are typically declared or easily detected, thus enabling model providers to manipulate the process, whether intentionally or inadvertently. papers.title: AI-Enabled Human Memory Manipulation: Misleading AI-Generated Summaries Distort Human Memory
papers.summary: AI-generated summaries and reports are increasingly used in high-stakes settings, like policing, despite considerable evidence that AI often generates misleading or inaccurate information. This research asked: do errors in AI-generated summaries distort human memory? To answer this question, we adopted two methodological approaches.
